ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the single machine infinite bus system shown below, the generator is delivering the real power of 0.8 p.u at 0.8 power factor lagging to the infinite bus. The power angle of the generator in degrees (round off to one decimal place) is ________
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a single-machine infinite bus system. On the left is generator G, after the generator is marked transient/synchronous reactance Xd = 0.25 pu, followed by a transformer reactance Xt = 0.2 pu in series. Between the middle and the infinite bus on the right there are two parallel transmission lines, and the upper and lower lines are both marked XL1 = 0.4 pu and XL2 = 0.4 pu. The voltage of the infinite bus on the right is marked V = 1∠0°. Reasoning: The two 0.4 pu lines are in parallel, so the equivalent reactance is 0.4 || 0.4 = 0.2 pu. Therefore, the total reactance from the generator internal potential to the infinite bus is Xeq = 0.25 + 0.2 + 0.2 = 0.65 pu. The problem gives that the generator transmits active power P = 0.8 pu to the infinite bus, with power factor 0.8 lagging, so the power factor angle phi = cos^-1(0.8), and the reactive power Q = P tan(phi) = 0.8 × 0.75 = 0.6 pu. Therefore the complex power S = 0.8 + j0.6 pu. Taking the infinite bus voltage V = 1∠0° as reference, from S = V I* we get I = 0.8 - j0.6 pu. The generator internal potential E = V + jXeq I = 1 + j(0.65)(0.8 - j0.6) = 1.39 + j0.52 pu. The generator power angle is the phase angle of E relative to the infinite bus voltage, namely delta = atan(0.52/1.39) = 20.5°, taken to one decimal place as 20.5°.

raw_record.question_text: In the single machine infinite bus system shown below, the generator is delivering the real power of 0.8 p.u at 0.8 power factor lagging to the infinite bus. The power angle of the generator in degrees (round off to one decimal place) is ________

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a generator connected through Xd = 0.25 pu and Xt = 0.2 pu to two parallel 0.4 pu lines feeding an infinite bus V = 1∠0°. Reduce the two lines: 0.4 || 0.4 = 0.2 pu, so total reactance from generator internal emf to the infinite bus is Xeq = 0.25 + 0.2 + 0.2 = 0.65 pu. From the text, P = 0.8 pu at pf = 0.8 lagging, so phi = cos^-1(0.8), Q = 0.8 tan(phi) = 0.6 pu, hence S = 0.8 + j0.6 pu delivered. With V = 1∠0°, use S = V I* to get I = 0.8 - j0.6 pu. Then compute E = V + jXeq I = 1 + j(0.65)(0.8 - j0.6) = 1.39 + j0.52. The required power angle is delta = angle(E) relative to the infinite bus, i.e. atan(0.52/1.39), then round to one decimal degree.
